home.title: Ouroboros
home.subtitle: Charitable foundation
home.description: From the south of Ukraine, we are standing up for one another — using art, mutual aid, and collective care to resist the violence of war and build solidarity from the ground up.

about.title: About Us
about.text:
We are a grassroots collective based in the south of Ukraine, specifically in Mykolaiv and Kherson, born out of urgency and sustained by care. When the full-scale invasion began, many of us were artists, businesspeople and organizers — but the war pushed us to come together in new ways. We are a multinational team. Our core members come both from the US and from Ukraine.
Oro, one of the founders of the organisation, was a professional photographer, artist and activist in the US before 2022 when he moved to Ukraine. He was drawn here not only by personal sentiment, as several of his close friends had already lived here or volunteered, but also by an innate sense of justice and duty. At first, he volunteered all over Ukraine, documenting war crimes, procuring and delivering humanitarian aid to front-line communities and supporting various military units. He has witnessed firsthand the horrors of russian aggression. He has worked in the east and south with several international organizations and has been living and volunteering in Ukraine for three years now.
Lyn, co-founder of the organization, a native Ukrainian and artist, first attended various volunteer initiatives in Lviv. Her desire to do and see more led her to humanitarian actions in the frontline areas in eastern Ukraine, and later to the south after meeting Oro at a friend’s memorial. Lyn is a talented multi-disciplinary artist, and recognizes the healing power of the arts in building community and healing traumas inflicted by war.
At the end of 2024, Oro and Lyn founded their organization — the Ouroboros Charitable Foundation. While humanitarian aid remains an important part of their work, the foundation now focuses on long-term needs that are just as urgent: supporting the psychological well-being of people affected by war, maintaining disaster readiness, and providing aid to vulnerable populations.
Sadly, every part of Ukraine continues to bear the deep trauma of conflict. Ouroboros has several socially vital projects, such as providing safe shelter and relocation for internally displaced people from high-risk areas of the Kherson region, helping people integrate into new communities, and developing initiatives to revitalize local economies.

project1.title: Humanitarian Aid for Frontline Communities
project1.description:
We work in southern Ukraine, helping villagers in the war-torn Kherson and Mykolaiv regions. Our team brings food, hygiene products, school supplies, and medical aid to people in need, even with daily shelling. Alongside local volunteers, we quickly respond to urgent requests.
With support from international donors, we get humanitarian aid to where it’s needed most. Our transparent network and local know-how help us work efficiently in both regions. In just our first six months, we’ve helped over 5,000 people and keep delivering aid where it’s still desperately needed.

project2.title: Support for Street Animals and Local Shelters
project2.description:
War doesn't just hurt people, it leaves behind thousands of animals too. In places like Kherson and Mykolaiv, there are many stray cats and dogs because their owners had to leave or were killed. Without proper care or spaying/neutering, the problem keeps getting worse.
We team up with local volunteers who bravely look after these animals despite the dangers and limited supplies. With our partners and donations, we deliver food and essentials to help villagers affected by the war in Kherson and Mykolaiv regions, and we also support a shelter in Mykolaiv to keep their work going strong.

project3.title: Supporting Communities Through Art and Connection
project3.description:
Recovering from the effects of war takes more than just aid, it takes people coming together, expressing creativity, and building care. That’s why we support the creation and operation of local community centers in frontline towns and villages, like the Mykolaiv art centre. With help from our international partners and donors, we provide these spaces with essentials like furniture, art supplies, and educational materials.
In summer 2025, the Mykolaiv art centre hosted an inspiring art camp led by artists, offering classes in painting, sculpture, and LARP-inspired activities. These creative sessions, guided by skilled artists, were designed to encourage self-expression, foster joy, and support emotional well-being for participants, especially children and families facing the challenges of war. The camp created a space for participants to explore their creativity, connect with others, and find moments of relief and inspiration.
These centers provide safe, welcoming spaces where people can gather, relax, and rebuild their sense of community. We organize regular events, workshops, and art-based activities to boost spirits, promote emotional resilience, and strengthen social bonds.

vision.title: Our Vision
vision.mainText: We envision a Ukraine where healing, dignity, and solidarity guide recovery from war.
vision.extendedText: We envision a Ukraine where healing, dignity, and solidarity guide recovery from war. Through community-rooted care, creative expression, and support for displaced people, the Ouroboros Charitable Foundation works toward a future where all survivors of conflict have access to safety, belonging, and the resources they need to rebuild their lives.

mission.title: Our Mission
mission.mainText: To create inclusive spaces for healing, empowerment, and regeneration through art, community, and care.
mission.extendedText: To create inclusive spaces for healing, empowerment, and regeneration through art, community, and care. We support war-affected individuals — especially displaced people, youth, and veterans — by fostering creativity, rebuilding communities, and promoting long-term well-being.

project1.title: Creative & Healing Center
project1.description:
A space for healing, creativity, and rebuilding community in the shadow of war.
In southern Ukraine, war has torn apart homes, families, and futures. But even in the midst of destruction, people still seek connection, meaning, and hope. That’s why we’re creating the Creative & Healing Center — a safe, welcoming space where individuals affected by war can come together to recover, grow, and reimagine their lives through shared creativity and care.
This future center will serve displaced families, war survivors, veterans, young people, and local residents who carry the weight of trauma and uncertainty. It will offer:
Art therapy and creative workshops led by local and visiting artists
- Community events and collaborative projects that foster connection and purpose
- A gallery and performance space to share what’s created with the wider world
- A quiet room and recreational zones for rest and reflection
- A small co-working and volunteer hub to build local initiatives
- An inclusive, affordable café which will provide tasty food and employment opportunities for the people we serve.
Whether someone has fled home, lost loved ones, or is simply searching for stability, this center will provide tools for emotional healing and opportunities for cultural expression. It will also become a vital platform for building solidarity between displaced and local communities — through art, storytelling, and action.
This is a long-term vision rooted in grassroots experience, real relationships, and the resilience we witness every day.
With your support, we can turn this vision into a living, breathing reality.

project2.title: Eco-Settlement for Displaced Families
project2.description:
A vision for safe, sustainable homes and a new beginning — built together.
As the war in Ukraine continues, thousands of families remain displaced, many trapped in dangerous zones with nowhere to go. At the same time, Ukraine’s rural regions hold incredible potential: abandoned villages, existing homes, and open land — resources that can be restored and repurposed to provide not just shelter, but a future.
Our Eco-Settlement Project aims to do just that.
We will work to transform these forgotten places into vibrant, eco-friendly communities where displaced families can find stability, purpose, and hope. The settlements will combine free housing, community-driven renovation efforts, and job opportunities in sustainable farming, crafts, and local enterprise.
Through a mix of renovated village homes and modular shelters, we will provide immediate and long-term housing to those most in need — especially families, veterans, and people who’ve lost everything. Together with volunteers and residents, we’ll rebuild these spaces through traditional Ukrainian “toloka” (collective labor), reconnecting people not only with land, but with one another.
Each settlement will also include:
- Cultural and co-working spaces for education, skill-building, and healing
- Local economic initiatives, from eco-agriculture to small-scale tourism
- Recreational zones and safe environments for children and families
- Inclusive infrastructure for veterans, the elderly, and those with disabilities
In time, these communities will become self-sustaining eco-villages — places where displaced people aren’t just surviving, but growing, leading, and shaping their own futures. They will serve as models for post-war recovery rooted in sustainability, dignity, and collective care.
By investing in this project, you help us turn loss into life. Abandonment into belonging.
Let’s build something lasting — together.

aboutProject.title: Support the Project: Street Animal Support in Kherson and Mykolaiv
aboutProject.description:
Our Street Animal Support Project helps vulnerable street dogs and cats in frontline and affected areas of southern Ukraine, especially Kherson and Mykolaiv. Many animals have been abandoned or injured due to the war, and local volunteers — fearless and devoted — struggle to care for them with limited resources.  
## Project Goals:  
- Purchase quality pet food from local producers to support both street animals and the local economy.  
- Provide mobility aids such as wheelchairs for wounded dogs who have lost or injured their legs in conflict zones.  
- Support local shelters and volunteer groups feeding and caring for street animals daily.  
## Estimated Budget:  
**$2,000 USD**  
This covers regular pet food deliveries and the purchase and shipping of specialized wheelchairs for disabled dogs in Kherson.  
## Project Timeline:  
Until 30.11.2025  
### If the project cannot be fully realized or there are leftover funds:  
Remaining funds will be redirected to other urgent animal welfare and humanitarian aid initiatives for people from the frontline zones within our foundation’s work in the south of Ukraine.  
## Important Information for Donors:  
*By donating to this project, you agree that your contribution may be reallocated to other related projects if this campaign concludes, becomes inactive, or cannot proceed.*  
**Donations are non-refundable.**  
**Help us care for the forgotten paws of Kherson and Mykolaiv — support the street animals today!**
